This enzyme is subsequently targeted by a compound with the structure (+)-(5S,7R)-7-Ethoxy-12-Hydroxy-2-Oxo-20-Norabieta-1(10),8,11,13-Tetraene. The final step in this pathway involves the enzyme Neuropilin-2, indicating a possible regulatory or functional interaction between Leosibirone B and Neuropilin-2. The evidence suggests that Leosibirone B may act as a modulator of the sialyltransferase pathway, potentially influencing the expression or activity of Neuropilin-2. The strength of this relationship is supported by the cumulative evidence of target engagement across the pathway, though the exact mechanism of interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
